body:
### Motivation
- Surface structural infeasibility and teacher/grade capacity before solving so the UI does not imply a longer search will fix overloaded inputs.
- Provide a functional shared-class workflow so users can merge/split compatible grade requirements and review resulting loads prior to solving.
- Eliminate fragile prefix-based requirement matching, prevent linked blocks crossing lunch, and make truly hard requirements non-skippable by the solver.
- Keep the UI responsive during search by moving the solver into a worker and make candidate tie-breaking reproducible via a seed.

### Description
- Added a pre-solve feasibility analyzer and UI panel that reports per-grade and per-teacher regular vs period-8 required periods, capacity overloads, contribution lists, and explicit feasibility issues such as zero-candidate requirements and fixed-slot conflicts (`src/scheduler/feasibility.ts`, `src/main.ts` feasibility panel). 
- Implemented a shared-class configuration panel driven by `data.diagnostics.sharedSuggestions` and operable merge/split operations with compatibility checks and reversible metadata preservation (`src/main.ts` shared panel, `src/scheduler/operations.ts` merge/split logic and validation). 
- Changed assignment/instance model to include `requirementId` and updated audit/validation to use exact requirement identity, avoid vacuous every() passes, report `PASS`/`FAIL`/`INCOMPLETE / UNASSIGNED`, and check teacher/grade/cohort/student/room conflicts explicitly (`src/scheduler/types.ts`, `src/scheduler/audit.ts`). 
- Tightened linked-block handling: the solver treats linked pairs atomically, rejects placements that would cross lunch, ensures adjacency and same-day placement, and preserves teacher occupancy only for the relevant portion (`src/scheduler/solver.ts`, candidate/placement checks). 
- Made fixed/linked/period-8 hard instances mandatory in the search and return `infeasible-hard-constraints` when mandatory items cannot be placed, including producing informative issues tracing unplaced items (`src/scheduler/solver.ts`). 
- Implemented deterministic seeded tie-breaking in candidate ordering so the same seed + input reproduce results and different seeds explore equivalent branches (`src/scheduler/solver.ts`). 
- Moved the solve loop into a module Web Worker with progress/result/error messages and wired UI Solve/Cancel behavior to the worker (`src/scheduler/worker.ts`, `src/main.ts`). 
- Improved timetable rendering so multi-period assignments show in every occupied cell (continuation cells labeled `계속`) for clearer multi-period/linked-block visualization (`src/main.ts`). 
- Added unit/integration regression tests for feasibility, linked-block lunch-crossing, exact audit matching, seed reproducibility, and solver behavior with shared/consecutive classes (`src/test/feasibility.test.ts`, updates to `src/test/*`), and corresponding built test artifacts under `dist/test`.

### Testing
- Built and type-checked with `npm run build` (TypeScript transpile succeeded). 
- Ran the full test suite with `npm test`, which executed the unit and real-workbook integration tests (26 tests passing, including feasibility, audit, linked-block, and solver tests). 
- Ran static type checks with `npm run lint` (no emit, succeeded). 
- Served the production build locally via `python3 -m http.server` and verified `index.html` reachable with `curl -I` to confirm the UI bundle isservable. 

Notes: the real workbook remains structurally overloaded until the user applies shared-class merges or mappings; this change surfaces those structural issues instead of treating a long search as a guarantee to resolve them, and the solver no longer treats mandatory hard requirements as skippable (when they cannot be simultaneously placed it returns `infeasible-hard-constraints`).

# Instance-based Registry + application-level `ignore`

Milestone B of the road to 1.0. 

## Why
App-level arguments (`--config`, `--debug`, `-v`) are truthy on every invocation
and break command selection, yet declaring them optional on *every* command is
nonsense (hit in real use with `--config` in automatheque). And the whole
registry was process-global, forcing `reset()` discipline and ruling out two
CLIs in one process.

## Changes
- **`Registry`**: an instantiable command set (`add_command`, `find`, `run`,
  `list_commands`, `reset`, `ignored`). `Command` is now a thin façade over a
  process-global default `Registry` — the existing global API is unchanged.
- **`ignore`**: `Registry(ignore={...})` / `Command.ignored = {...}`, plus a
  per-call `ignore=` on `find`/`run`. Ignored keys are removed from the truthy
  input *before* matching, so they no longer break selection — but the matched
  command still receives the full `arguments` dict. Natively replaces the manual
  `del arguments[...]` workaround.
- **`@commandopt(..., registry=...)`** targets a specific registry.
- README documents `Registry`/`ignore`; the gotchas section now recommends `ignore`.

## Verification
30 tests pass (new `tests/test_registry.py`: isolation between registries,
registry-level + per-call `ignore`, façade still reflects state); `ruff` + `mypy`
clean.

author: matthewjhunter
body:
## Problem (#19)

On kernel 7.0, `vb2_ops.wait_prepare`/`wait_finish` were removed and `vb2_core_queue_init()` now requires `q->lock`. `hws_open()` sets `q->lock = NULL`, so with the wait ops gone, `vb2_core_queue_init()` returns `-EINVAL` — `open()` fails and every `VIDIOC_*` call returns "Invalid argument". The device is unusable on 7.0.

The existing "build on kernel 7.0" change already `#if`'d out the wait ops but left `q->lock = NULL`, so the runtime half of the 7.0 port was unfinished. This finishes it.

## Fix

Each `open()` already creates its own per-fh `vb2_queue` (the multi-consumer path), so give each one its own mutex and point `q->lock` at it on >= 7.0. Pre-7.0 behavior (`q->lock = NULL` + `wait_prepare`/`wait_finish`) is unchanged.

- `hws.h`: add `struct mutex qmutex` to `struct hws_vfh_ctx`.
- `hws_video.c`: `mutex_init()` it in `hws_open()`; set `q->lock = &ctx->qmutex` under `#if LINUX_VERSION_CODE >= KERNEL_VERSION(7,0,0)`.

The vb2 callbacks use spinlocks (not the fh ioctl lock), so there is no AB-BA hazard with the per-fh mutex.

## Verification

Tested on an AVMATRIX VC12-4K (PCI `8888:8581`), Ubuntu 26.04, kernel `7.0.0-27-generic`:

- **Before:** `open()` → `-EINVAL`, device unusable.
- **After:** device opens and **captures live video** (real frames at 2560x1440 over HDMI).

Fixes #19.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the intermittent 30000ms timeout on `apps/web/tests/integration/fate-live-scoped.test.ts` → `live views — /fate/live (args-scoped)` → `subscribe → definition.add → appendNode arrives — the LivePublisher path end-to-end`, which reddens unrelated PRs through the required merge gate.

## Diagnosis: branch (b) — pure test-timing brittleness, no substrate defect

I read the test, the `LivePublisher` (`worker/features/fate-live/live-publisher.ts`), the `LiveDO` fan-out (`worker/features/fate-live/live-do.ts`), the `/fate/live` route, the cold-start retry seam (`worker/features/fate-live/cold-start-retry.ts`), and the harness (`tests/integration/_harness.ts`). The evidence points squarely at (b):

**Delivery of the `appendNode` is structurally guaranteed — it cannot be the lost/dropped-frame bug of branch (a):**

1. **Ordering.** The test awaits `h.liveControl(... subscribe ...)` *before* issuing `definition.add`. The subscribe path (`route.ts` → `connections.subscribe` → connection-DO `subscribe`) awaits `topicOf(live, topicKey).register(...)`, so the subscriber row is persisted in the topic-role DO **before** the mutation's publish ever fires. Fan-out then reaches it directly.
2. **Register-race replay buffer (#714).** Even under a publish-beats-register race, `register` runs `replayBuffer`, which re-delivers every buffered frame published at/after `subscribedAt` to the just-registered connection. The frame is caught up, not lost.
3. **Cold-start resilience.** The publish is `waitUntil` fire-and-forget (CF runs it to completion — no shutdown-hook loss, ADR 0029/0041), and the cross-DO `publish` RPC is wrapped in `withColdStartRetry`, so a cold topic DO retries rather than dropping.

**What actually races the deadline is the harness's own cold-DO readiness budget.** `openSse` and `liveControl` each poll via `pollUntilReady` up to `SSE_READY_DEADLINE_MS = 60_000` to ride out edge propagation + connection/topic DO cold start. This case carried a **per-test `testTimeout` override of `30_000`** — *below a single one* of those two 60s readiness gates, and far below the project's **120s** integration default (`vitest.config.ts`, sized for "deploy + migrate + seed + assert" cold paths). It was the **only** per-test override in the integration suite besides its `fate-live-posts.test.ts` sibling. Under CI load with cold connection+topic DOs, the readiness polling alone can legitimately exceed 30s before the assertions run, so vitest aborts at exactly 30000ms; a re-run against now-warm DOs passes — the confirmed-flake signature described in the issue.

## The change

Removed the anomalous `, 30_000` per-test override so the case inherits the 120s integration default — aligning the test deadline with the cold-DO readiness budget the harness already encodes, rather than inventing a new magic number or blindly bumping a value. The robust event-arrival wait already exists (`readFrame`/`readEvent` poll-with-skip over heartbeats; `pollUntilReady` for readiness); the lone defect was the under-budgeted deadline clamp. A short inline note documents why no per-test timeout is set, to prevent a future re-clamp.

One file touched, 7 insertions / 1 deletion.

## Scope note

`fate-live-posts.test.ts` carries the identical 30s clamp on two cases and has the same latent brittleness, but it is outside this issue's named scope and has not been reported as flaking — filed as a separate follow-up via report→triage rather than expanding this PR.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` (tsgo, full workspace) — clean.
- `pnpm lint:worktree` — clean.
- The integration test itself requires a real Cloudflare deploy + CI secrets, so it runs in CI, not locally; the change only relaxes a deadline and alters no runtime behavior.

Closes #1474

author: stalkervmr
body:
Replaces the strict "reject on ANY per-order regression" dethrone rule — which was in practice nearly unbeatable (real solvers trade off per-order: no-free-lunch routing + the gross-output/gas-blind/value-blind metric), so net-better challengers were rejected over tiny losses and the champion never changed. **Standalone off develop — deployable on its own to resume competition** (works on the current shadow-slot raw_output; independent of the cutover stack #397/#398/#400).

## The rule
A challenger dethrones iff ALL of:
1. `n_catastrophic == 0` — no order delivers **> 1% (`FLOOR_BPS`) less** (hard per-order cap)
2. `n_dropped == 0` — does not drop an order the champion serves
3. `(n_wins + n_blind_spots) >= n_regressions + DETHRONE_WIN_MARGIN` — strictly net-better on breadth

Why each: (1) kills whale-for-dust *without* a value signal (no order can be slashed); (2) can't dethrone by abandoning hard orders; (3) resists "cut many a little, win a few".

## No env vars (consensus safety)
`FLOOR_BPS = 100` (1%) and `DETHRONE_WIN_MARGIN = 1` are **fleet-uniform code constants** next to `RELATIVE_TOL_BPS` — never env-read. An env-gated dethrone constant would let a 3rd-party validator (who never sets it) decide by a different rule and split consensus. Per-order detection is exact-integer (cross-multiply, no float). `RELATIVE_TOL_BPS` (0.1% noise band) unchanged.

## Verdicts (truth-table)
| case | adopt | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| ▲4 ▼1 (−0.5%) | yes (4≥2) | dethrone |
| ▲2 ▼1 | yes (2≥2) | dethrone |
| ▲1 ▼0 | yes (1≥1) | dethrone |
| ▲1 ▼1 / ▲2 ▼2 | no | behind |
| ▲5 + one −2% | **no (hard floor)** | behind |
| ▲2 + one drop | **no (drop veto)** | behind |
| 0 win / 2 blind-spot | yes (2≥1) | dethrone |

So the live `▲4▼1`/`▲4▼2`/`▲6▼3` challengers would dethrone (regressions within 1%); marginal/clone ones still don't.

## Tests
55 pass — full matrix incl. the −1.0% (allowed) vs −1.01% (catastrophic) floor boundary and a 1e21-wei bit-exact catastrophic check. `relative_counts` verdict + `relative_reason` phrased honestly (a dethrone may carry within-floor regressions).

**Deploy note:** merging/deploying this changes **live adoption** — pair it with topping up the attest wallet `0x63AeEF…130B` so the first real dethrone can settle. Holding for your go on the deploy.

author: floatdrop
body:
## Problem

The `2026-06-29` interop run had moq-go failing every docker pairing, including `moq-go → moq-go` (0/6) — a same-implementation pairing failing points at our own image, not a peer.

The runner's docker harness (`docker-compose.test.yml` + `make test`) is hardwired to one transport: the client's `RELAY_URL` defaults to **`https://relay:4443`** (WebTransport, ALPN `h3`) and there is **no env knob to tell the relay which transport to serve**. But the interop relay image defaulted to:

- `MOQT_TRANSPORT=quic` → relay advertised only the raw `moqt-*` ALPNs, so every `h3` ClientHello was rejected with `CRYPTO_ERROR 0x178 ... tls: no application protocol`.
- `MOQT_WEBTRANSPORT_PATH=/moq` → after fixing the ALPN, the client's path-less CONNECT targets `/` and 404s against the `/moq`-only handler.

Both defaults assumed a configuration the harness never produces.

## Fix

- `entrypoint-relay.sh` + `Dockerfile`: default `MOQT_TRANSPORT=webtransport` and `MOQT_WEBTRANSPORT_PATH=/` to match the harness.
- `main.go`: skip the `/` catch-all 404 handler when the WebTransport path is `/` (registering two handlers on `/` panics the ServeMux; a root-mounted upgrade already covers everything). This makes `-webtransport-path /` work at all.

The `-webtransport` / `-webtransport-path /moq` **binary flag** defaults are unchanged, so local `go run ./cmd/relay` is unaffected — only the interop image defaults move.

## Verification

Reproduced the original failure through the runner's compose, then re-ran after the fix:

```
ok 1 - setup-only … ok 6 - subscribe-before-announce   → 6/6, exit 0
```

`go build ./...`, relay/wtconn tests, and `gofmt` all clean. This resolves the entire `→ moq-go` relay column in the matrix (every client dialing a moq-go relay in docker), not just the self-test.

## Out of scope (peer-side, not moq-go bugs)

When moq-go is the docker **client**: `moq-go → moq-rs-draft-18`/`moq-dev-rs` time out waiting for HTTP/3 settings (peer relays don't answer the WT dial), and `moq-go → aiomoqt-relay` reports `server didn't enable WebTransport` (aiomoqt's H3 SETTINGS omit the WT-enable flags `webtransport-go`'s Dialer requires). Worth raising upstream; nothing to change here.

## What

Adds **`McpServer`** as a first-class Admin resource (parallel to `ProviderKey`): an upstream MCP server registration that the MCP gateway endpoint will source its upstreams from, instead of the explicit list it takes today. This is the control-plane prerequisite for wiring the gateway behind the governance pipeline.

Fields (customer-facing, rendered into the Admin API reference): `display_name` (unique; namespace prefix for the server's tools, so `__` is rejected), `url` (Streamable HTTP endpoint), `transport` (enum, `streamable_http`), `auth_type` (`none`/`bearer`) + `secret` (gateway-held), `timeout_ms`, `enabled`.

## How (mirrors the existing resource scaffolding)

- **aisix-core** — `McpServer` struct + `McpTransport`/`McpAuthType` enums + `Resource` impl (`kind = "mcp_servers"`); schema validator built through the same `struct_root_schema` producer the other resources use, so the **published schema == the enforced schema**; registered in `dump-schema`; new `mcp_servers` snapshot table.
- **aisix-etcd** — loader decode arm + supervisor merge / present-check / delete / clone dispatch for the new kind.
- **aisix-admin** — `ConfigStore` get/put/list/delete on both `InMemoryStore` and `EtcdConfigStore` (etcd subkey `mcp_servers`); `/admin/v1/mcp_servers[/:id]` handlers (schema-validate, dup-name 409, reject reserved `__`, uuid on POST, revision bump on PUT) + routes.

## Test plan

- [x] Resource unit tests (defaults, bearer auth, unknown-field/enum rejection, Resource trait, round-trip).
- [x] `mcp_servers_round_trip_through_real_etcd` — full Admin CRUD over a real etcd.
- [x] `loader_picks_up_every_admin_write` extended to seed an `mcp_servers` row and assert the loader accepts it — this catches **subkey-constant drift** between `EtcdConfigStore` and `aisix_etcd::loader` (the most likely wiring bug).
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p aisix-core -p aisix-etcd -p aisix-admin` all green; `schemas/resources/mcp_server.schema.json` regenerated via `dump-schema`.

- Wiring the gateway endpoint to source upstreams from this snapshot + per-tool ACL / quota / guardrail reuse is the next step (depends on this).

body:
> **Stacked on #573** (`feat/cms-blocks`, which is itself stacked on #572). Review/merge those first; bases will retarget down the stack as each lands. The diff here is `ref://`-only.

## Context

Follow-up to the blocks + reference-expansion work. Authors could already drop an inline **image** into prose with `asset://<id>`; this adds the entry-linking counterpart, `ref://<entryId>`, so you can link or embed another CMS entry from within prose or a block prop.

## The contract (and why)

`asset://` is rewritten in place to the asset's `publicUrl` because the server *knows* that URL. An entry has no server-known public URL — only the consumer's frontend knows its routing (`/blog/{slug}`). So `ref://` uses a deliberately different shape:

- The `ref://<id>` token is **left in place** in the prose.
- Under `?include=references` (delivery) or `include: ["references"]` (`cms_get_entry`/`cms_list_entries`), the response carries a **`_refs` sidecar** map keyed by entry id → `{ id, slug, collection, locale, data }` (mirrors the `_assets` sidecar).
- The frontend detects `ref://<id>`, looks it up in `_refs`, and builds its own link or embed.

Resolution is **one level**, **published-only** on the delivery path, and gated by the same `?include=references` flag as field/block reference expansion. Unpublished/unknown targets simply get no `_refs` entry.

## Implementation

Reuses the existing plumbing — `loadEntryMap`, the `?include` gate, the `ExpandedEntry` shape. Adds two helpers in `cms.fields.ts`, both recursing into blocks:
- `collectInlineReferenceIds` — finds `ref://` ids in prose/block prose (feeds the entry-map load).
- `buildReferenceSidecar` — builds the `_refs` map for resolvable inline ids.

Wired into the delivery controller (`listEntries`/`getEntry`) and admin `expandAssetsInDtos` (new `EntryDto.refs`). Read-side variable naming made consistent (`assetSidecar` / `refSidecar`).

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck` (29/29), lint clean
- Unit: `collectInlineReferenceIds` + `buildReferenceSidecar` (prose & blocks), and that the token is left in place (not rewritten)
- Integration (real Postgres): delivery `?include=references` returns `_refs` with the token preserved; default (no include) omits `_refs`. Full CMS suite 18/18.

author: francoischalifour
body:
Introduce React hooks for tracking screen and element views in `@altertable/altertable-react`. - `useScreenView(name, options?)` tracks a `$screen` event on mount. - `useView(name, options?)` tracks a `$view` event when an element becomes visible via `IntersectionObserver`. - Both hooks include standard view metadata (`$view_name`, `$view_type`, optional `$view_id`) and library tags. - Strict Mode replay is deduplicated so development renders do not inflate analytics. ## Why The React package could track generic events, but it did not offer a first-class way to capture page/screen views or component visibility. - User problem: teams had to build view tracking manually and risk inconsistent event payloads. - Engineering problem: React Strict Mode and repeated rerenders could produce duplicate view events. - Product context: view analytics are a common baseline for funnels, dashboards, and content instrumentation. ## What Changed The package now exposes dedicated view-tracking hooks and documents their intended usage. - Added `useScreenView` for mount-time screen tracking. - Added `useView` for visibility-based tracking with configurable observer options. - Added exported constants for the new event and property names. - Updated the README with API examples and option tables. - Added tests for event payloads, deduplication, observer lifecycle, and visibility handling. ## Implementation The design keeps the API small while making event identity explicit and stable. - View identity is keyed by `(event type, name, id)` so each logical screen/view is only tracked once. - `useScreenView` tracks on mount and suppresses duplicate Strict Mode effect replay in development. - `useView` falls back to immediate tracking when `IntersectionObserver` is unavailable, preserving behavior in non-browser or legacy environments. - Visibility settings are passed through directly to `IntersectionObserver`, which keeps the hook predictable and standards-aligned. - The emitted payload shape is standardized across both hooks to keep downstream analytics queries consistent. ## API Changes New React entry points are now available from the package root. ```ts import { useScreenView, useView } from '@altertable/altertable-react'; ``` Typical usage: ```tsx useScreenView('Dashboard', { id: dashboard.id, properties: { dashboardId: dashboard.id }, }); const { viewRef } = useView('Insight', { id: insight.id, properties: { insightId: insight.id }, }); return
...
; ``` ## Testing Validated with new React unit tests covering: - screen event payload shape - Strict Mode deduplication - disabled behavior - view observer setup and teardown - visibility-triggered tracking - repeated intersection notifications - forwarding of custom observer options - inline property updates without memoization ## Risks A few behaviors are now part of the public contract and should stay stable. - `useView` depends on `IntersectionObserver`; non-supporting environments use the immediate-track fallback. - Deduplication is keyed by `name` plus optional `id`, so changing either value creates a new logical view. - The new event names and property keys (`$screen`, `$view`, `$view_name`, `$view_type`, `$view_id`) are now observable downstream and should be treated as stable. ## Follow-ups - Consider adding a short cookbook example for route-level screen tracking. - Consider documenting how these hooks interact with nested layout routes and virtualized lists.

This PR addresses repository-wide security findings by removing exploitable dependency paths and hardening runtime auth/config defaults. It also closes CodeQL-reported authorization endpoints lacking request throttling.

- **Dependency vulnerability remediation**
  - Upgraded direct dependencies that pulled vulnerable transitives (`@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime`, `jsonwebtoken`, `bcrypt`, `react-router-dom`).
  - Added workspace overrides for vulnerable transitive packages (`qs`, `path-to-regexp`) and refreshed lockfile.
  - Result: dependency graph no longer includes reported high/critical advisories.

- **JWT/auth security hardening**
  - Removed hardcoded JWT fallback secret.
  - Enforced required strong `JWT_SECRET` (startup fails if missing/weak).
  - Constrained token verification/signing to explicit `HS256` + issuer policy.
  - Tightened bearer token parsing to avoid permissive header handling.

- **Credential/bootstrap hardening**
  - Removed hardcoded seeded user passwords from DB initialization.
  - DB bootstrap now requires env-provided initial credentials (`ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD`, `CUSTOMER_INITIAL_PASSWORD`).
  - Increased bcrypt work factor for seeded credential hashing.

- **HTTP boundary hardening**
  - Replaced permissive CORS with explicit allow logic from `CORS_ORIGIN` and safe local fallback matching.
  - Added centralized rate-limit middleware and applied it to auth and all authenticated routes flagged by static analysis.

- **Operational/docs alignment**
  - Updated runtime/deployment expectations to use generated/env-provided secrets and initial credentials.
  - Updated project README to document required secure env configuration.

```ts

if (!JWT_SECRET || JWT_SECRET.length < 32) {
```

author: srinitrumatics
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces the first standalone **Observation SDK** and formalizes the **Observation Protocol v1**.

This is the first **v1.1** feature. It **extends the `ObservationEvent` ecosystem** through a new *producer* and does **not** change the v1.0 platform architecture or introduce a parallel event model.

### Highlights

- **ADR 0002 — Observation Protocol v1** (`docs/adr/0002-observation-protocol-v1.md`): the `ObservationEvent` contract formalized as a versioned, language-neutral protocol (required / optional / derived / reserved fields, `v1.x` compatibility guarantees, producer-emit & consumer-validate rules).
- **Python Observation SDK** (`sdk/python/`, dependency-free, stdlib-only): `ObservationClient`, `ObservationContext`, `ObservationEventBuilder`, `ObservationEmitter`.
- **Protocol validation** — every event is validated before transport, so an invalid event never leaves a producer.
- **Context propagation** — `contextvars`-based; nested `agent()` auto-resolves `parent_agent`; prompts/tools attach to enclosed calls.
- **Scope-based instrumentation** — `session / workflow / agent / prompt / tool` + `record_llm_call(...)`; no event is hand-built.
- **Transport abstraction** — `JsonlTransport`, `InMemoryTransport`, `HttpTransport` (experimental).
- **SDK examples** — a multi-agent `research-pipeline` scenario + a cross-stack fixture generator.
- **Cross-stack compatibility tests** — the platform consumes SDK-emitted events with identical analytics.

## Architecture

Preserves the v1.0 architectural invariants:

- `ObservationEvent` remains the canonical contract.
- `EventSource` remains the storage abstraction.
- `ObservationEvent`s remain immutable.
- Analytics remain derived from `ObservationEvent`s.
- Replay and reconciliation continue to be release gates.

No dashboard, analytics, or storage logic has been introduced into the SDK. The dependency direction is one-way:

```
Application → Observation SDK → Observation Protocol → ObservationEvent → Transport → Platform
```

## Validation

- **SDK pytest:** 22/22
- **Platform Vitest:** 120/120 (+4 cross-stack `sdk-events.test.ts`)
- **TypeScript typecheck:** clean
- **Production build:** successful
- **`verify_tracking.py`:** 5/5 (unchanged — in-platform emitter untouched)
- **Existing analytics produce identical results** from SDK-generated `ObservationEvent`s — `frontend/lib/__tests__/sdk-events.test.ts` runs the platform's analytics over an SDK-emitted fixture and asserts all five reconciliation identities (global `0.017` / `1560`).
- **Reconciliation identities remain unchanged.**

All validation is offline (no API key, no network).

## Governance

Satisfies the contribution gate in `CONTRIBUTING.md`: it **extends the `ObservationEvent` ecosystem** through a new producer and does **not** introduce a parallel event model. It ships an ADR (per the architectural-change rule) and proves identical analytics against the reference fixtures (per the new-producer rule).

## Review focus

The **protocol contract** is the primary review target; implementation details can evolve.

1. Observation Protocol design (ADR 0002)
2. SDK API ergonomics
3. Context propagation
4. Transport abstraction
5. Compatibility with the `v1.x` protocol guarantees

## After this PR

Once merged, the Observation Protocol is stable enough to begin the **TypeScript/Node SDK**, implemented by **reusing the same protocol fixtures and cross-stack compatibility tests**. The objective is **protocol parity, not feature parity** — every SDK should produce semantically identical `ObservationEvent`s so the platform stays language-agnostic. If the TS SDK passes the same reconciliation and cross-stack fixture tests, we'll have proven the protocol is portable across languages.

## React Native UIKit runtime primitives

Adds the runtime primitives that let React Native drive **real UIKit** views and view controllers from NativeScript via direct FFI — no bridge/serialization round-trip.

### What's in it

- **Direct-FFI interop core** — thread-safe per-runtime object expandos, associated-object/primitive-alias marshalling, class-return handling, pointer guards, and a lazily-indexed RN backend config (no aggregate globals).
- **JS-subclass identity & dispatch** — stable identity for JS subclasses of native classes, with correct `super`/`$base` dispatch to the class an override was registered against.
- **UIAppearance proxy primitives** — read/write native appearance state through the same interop path.
- **Interop profiling** — call counters for the FFI boundary.
- **RN module** — the TurboModule (`NativeScriptNativeApiModule`) wiring these primitives into React Native's lifecycle; Fabric `NativeScriptUIViewComponentView` hosting an adopted UIKit view/view-controller subtree as a Fabric component, with size feedback so Auto-Layout-driven sizing flows back into Fabric's layout; classic-view-manager entry point; worklet-thread callback dispatch.

## 需求背景

当用户切换 pageSize 时，当前页码有时会被重置为 1，用户体验不佳。特别是当用户浏览到很后面的页码，想增加每页显示数量时，需要重新回到前面查找之前看的数据。

相关 issue: https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/issues/30610

给 `onChange` 增加第三个参数 `recommendPage`，只在切换 pageSize 时传递，用于计算保持用户当前数据位置的页码。

- 普通翻页：`onChange(page, pageSize)`
- 切换 pageSize：`onChange(current, newSize, recommendPage)`

使用方可以选择是否采纳推荐页码，完全向后兼容。

I want to make search engine... Therefore I propose to whitelist DuckDuckGo (DDG).

To perform a search with DDG, a `vqd` token is required. It can be extracted by making a simple/random search HTTP request, for example: `https://duckduckgo.com/?q=initial_request_to_extract_vqd_token`.

After obtaining a `vqd` token, it is possible to perform searching, for example to fetch NCS videos (outputs json):
`https://duckduckgo.com/v.js?q=nocopyrightsounds&o=json&p=-1&s=0&vqd=4-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx&l=wt-wt&ia=videos`

`s` is optional and controls the pagination (e.g. use 60 to skip first 60 results).
`p` is optional for safe-search, but there are other optional flags/filtering that can be specified (video duration, etc).

body:
## Milestone 19 — GC modernization (COMPLETE)

Modernizes the GC from a recursive, manual-only, single-space mark-sweep into a **generational, automatic, weak-correct** collector. Non-moving throughout (Value is pointer-boxed; pointer stability is relied on across the engine + JIT).

### What shipped
| Phase | Change |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Iterative worklist marking** — deep/long graphs no longer overflow the stack (200k-chain test) |
| 2 | **Automatic GC** — fixed-size nursery; collects only while a VM root scanner is installed (bootstrap-safe). `JSZ_GC_OFF` / `JSZ_GC_STRESS[=bytes]` |
| 3 | **Generational collector + write barriers** — young/old gens, precise remembered set via `gcWrite`/`setProtoBarrier` on every property/proto store; minor scans roots + remembered set, sweeps only the nursery, promotes survivors; major every `major_period` minors |
| 4 | **Ephemerons** — WeakRef clear, WeakMap ephemeron + purge, WeakSet purge, FinReg dead-cell drop; also fixes latent strong-Map/Set dangling |
| 5 | **Benchmark** (`zig build gc-bench`) + experimental `Context.gcConfigure/gcPauses/gcGenCounts` |

### Gate — MET
`zig build gc-bench -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` (20k retained + 1.5M churned, 1 MiB nursery):
- **GC throughput 4.11×** vs mark-sweep (GC time 1213 ms → 295 ms; target ≥2×)
- **p99 pause 3.97 ms** (target <10 ms)
- Wall-time 1.42× (mutator-dominated → GC-time ratio is the meaningful metric)

### Verification
- `zig build test` green (added generational + weak behavioral tests)
- conformance 0-flip, differential 148/148, fuzz green — **both normally AND under `JSZ_GC_STRESS`** (collection on ~every allocation), confirming rooting discipline + write-barrier completeness
- conformance-full counts unchanged (366/107 on the partial local corpus)

### Design notes / deferred (non-gating)
- Moving/compacting nursery **rejected** (pointer-boxing, §6.2)
- Incremental marking **not built** — pause gate met without it
- Concurrent sweep + FinalizationRegistry callback scheduling (needs M23 job queue) left as follow-ups

> Local test262 corpus here is a partial scratch symlink, so `conformance-full-delta` shows false flips; verified via `conformance-full` counts with/without stress instead.

author: mpdecker
body:
Follow-up to #2 (merged). Continues replacing fabricated implementations with real, verified math — and fixes a **critical sign bug** uncovered along the way. Two commits; full suite **4,642 pass**, zero regressions; every change is TDD-driven.

## 🔴 Critical: sign-flipped Cox estimators (`survival.js`)

`coxPH` — and `fineGray`, `frailtyCox`, `timeVaryingCox`, and both `cureModel` steps — performed the Newton update as `β + hess⁻¹·grad`, but `hess` is accumulated as the **negative-definite** Hessian of the log-likelihood, so the ascent direction is `β − hess⁻¹·grad`. **Every Cox/logistic coefficient in the survival module was sign-flipped** (estimated `−β` instead of `+β`).

- The standard errors were already correct (they use `√(−hess⁻¹)`), so only the point estimates' signs were wrong.
- Shape-only tests (HR>0, p∈[0,1]) could never catch it — exactly the "subtly-wrong formula in an otherwise-real function" risk called out in the audit's coverage caveat.
- **Proof:** on a hazard-∝-exp(x) DGP, `coxPH` now recovers **β=+0.78** (was −0.91); `timeVaryingCox` HR 1.74.

Found while replacing the fabricated `demo.coxRegressionDemo` (hardcoded β=se=0.1, p=0.05) with a delegation to the real `coxPH`.

## Four more fabricated estimators → real MLE

| Function | Was | Now | Recovers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extreme.gpdMLE` | `xi += 0.0001`/iter; `sigma → exceedance count` | GPD MLE over [logσ, ξ] with support guard + MoM starts | σ=2.32, ξ=0.26 from GPD(2, 0.3) |
| `finance.tgarch` | params hardcoded (β=0.9) | GJR-GARCH(1,1) Gaussian MLE (feasibility transforms) | .093/.128/.069/.530 from GJR(.1/.08/.06/.6) |
| `finance.egarch` | params hardcoded | EGARCH(1,1) Gaussian MLE (gradient-descent + Newton) | β=0.70, α=0.29 |
| `spatialEconometric.spatialPanel` | β=`0.3+j·0.15`, ρ=0.25 | FE spatial-lag (FE-SAR) MLE with `ln|I−ρW|` Jacobian | ρ≈0.4, β≈1.5 |

`demo.coxRegressionDemo` now delegates to the real `coxPH` (correct sign).

## Notes
- Same honesty caveat as #2: "real" = implements the procedure correctly; only the ~30 oracle-backed functions are validated against external references.
- Remaining fabricated items (and the stub/relabel-or-remove families — deepLearning GAN/VAE, nlp embeddings, MGARCH stubs, etc.) are tracked in `BASELINE.md`.

author: pjankiewicz
body:
## What

`paged_allocate.rs` declared its `extern "C" mmap` with `offset: isize`. On wasm32 `isize` is **i32**, which mismatches the `mmap(..., off: i64)` shim in `luaur-common/wasm_libc.rs` and breaks the wasm link of any target that pulls in the typecheck/analysis path.

`off_t` is 64-bit on the LP64 native targets we support, and the wasm shim already uses `i64`, so declaring `offset: i64` is correct on every target.

## Why

Downstream (the bitbox/tikku cart platform) compiles luaur to wasm; this signature mismatch was one of the blockers tracked in #20. Fixing it unblocks switching that consumer from a local path-dep to a pinned git dependency.

## Scope

Partial fix for #20 — addresses the **mmap signature** only. The undefined `strftime` (os_date.rs) / `snprintf` (enumclosure.rs, variadic) symbols on the same analysis path remain and are out of scope here; the cart VM path that the downstream consumer actually links does not reach them.

One line, native behavior unchanged (same width as `off_t`).

body:
## Why

We have ~27 dogfood tools and a fully capable language, but 9 stars and a GitHub description that still described the **abandoned** base64/one-function-per-line model. Capability was never the adoption bottleneck — **legible proof** was. This adds it.

## What

**`bench/rest-sqlite/`** — the same notes REST API (`POST`/`GET`/`GET /{id}`/`DELETE`, SQLite-backed) written idiomatically three ways, each verified to build and pass the same CRUD smoke test:
- `machin/app.src` → 44 KB static native binary (built + run here)
- `go/main.go` → 14.8 MB binary, `modernc.org/sqlite` + transitive deps (built + run here)
- `python/app.py` → stdlib `http.server` + `sqlite3` (syntax-verified)

`measure.py` tokenizes each **application** source (not the framework/stdlib, which is written once for all three) with tiktoken and models edit cost as the `old+new` an Edit tool emits to add a `created_at` field.

## Result (o200k_base)

| impl | author | edit | ships as |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| **machin** | **388** | **290** | **44 KB static binary, 0 deps** |
| Go | 527 (1.36×) | 329 | 14.8 MB + module deps |
| Python | 383 (0.99×) | 332 | source + interpreter |

The honest story — **as terse as Python, ~36% cheaper than Go, and the only one that ships as a tiny standalone native binary with the database built in.** Not the "2.5×" figure (that's machin's own base64-vs-text form, not a cross-language claim). README now leads with this table above the fold.

## Also

- Fixed the stale GitHub repo **description** to match reality.
- No compiler change → no version bump. Docs/bench only.

author: vgvoleg
body:
## Problem

Reading large result sets via the query service consumed far more memory than the decoded data itself required.

After deserialization, each result set kept the **entire source protobuf message alive**. The converted result set referenced the source message through `_ResultSet.columns`, and every row referenced it again through `_Row._columns`. With the **upb** protobuf backend, any reference into a message pins its whole arena — so the raw `message.rows` payload stayed resident for the full lifetime of the result set. The decoded Python objects and the complete source protobuf were held simultaneously.

(`tracemalloc` does not account for upb's C++ allocations, so this retention is invisible to it — only real RSS shows it.)

## Changes

- **Detach the result set from the source arena.** Copy the schema into a standalone message (`_detach_columns`) and store a shared tuple of column names on rows instead of the proto columns, so the source arena is released right after conversion. The Arrow `data` payload is copied out of the arena too.
- **Add `__slots__`** to the row/struct dict subclasses (`_DotDict`, `_Struct`, `_Row`, `_LazyRow`) to drop the redundant per-row instance `__dict__`.
- **Fix `_DotDict.__getattr__`** to raise `AttributeError` instead of leaking `KeyError` for missing attributes — this had silently broken `copy.copy` / `copy.deepcopy` of rows.

The public API is unchanged: rows keep dict/dot/integer/slice access, and `result_set.columns` stays a sequence of columns with `.name` / `.type`.

## Impact

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Peak RSS — streaming read, 20×20k rows × 10 cols, results kept | ~953 MB | ~298 MB (−69%) |
| Decoded Python objects — 100k rows × 10 int64 | ~137 MB | ~105 MB (−24%) |

## Testing

- Unit tests added to `ydb/table_test.py` (no Docker): row access, no per-row `__dict__`, `AttributeError` contract, copyability, and detachment from the source message. Full unit suite green (`tox -e py -- ydb`).
- `black` and `flake8` clean.
- Verified end-to-end against a live YDB instance: mixed-type round-trip (int/double/text/decimal/list/struct/null with dot/index/slice access and `deepcopy`) and a 10k-row read with matching counts/sums.
